Subject: Renewal: Reserved GPU top-up + fallback/throughput guardrails

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the chat last week. Per our renewal timeline, attached is a concise proposal to add reserved capacity and put explicit fallback behavior in place so your svc remains responsive during spikes. Highlights: 

- Base change: +8 reserved A100-equivalent GPUs pooled across three clusters (regional pinning: primary us-west, failover us-east).
- Throughput target: 450 requests/min sustained per pool; 99th pct latency SLO 200ms token gen.
- Failover/fallback: two options described in the SOW (attached):
  • Firm-reserve + limited on-demand failover: 10% burst allowance above reserved capacity billed at on-demand rate; automatic cold-start failover to adjacent pool if regional saturation persists > 3m.
  • Lower base reserve + soft-fallback: higher on-demand grace; system applies progressive throttling and request-prioritization at 60% queue depth.

Attachment: [Attachment: SaaSify_Renewal_SOW_v3.pdf (PDF, 1.1MB)]

If you want, we can lock in throughput guarantees for the firm-reserve option and include credit-based remediation if we miss the SLA (we've priced the credit ladder in the SOW). Can you confirm whether the procurement team prefers a hard cap (no on-demand) or wants on-demand spill billing for bursts?

Proposed next step: quick 30-min sync with procurement + engineering to pick an option and sign SOW. Are you free this week?

Best,

Alex —

Thanks — we reviewed internally and put two explicit options in the attached SOW (summary below). Also included a 1-page runbook and paging list.

Option A — Firm-reserve + bounded failover (recommended for critical workloads):
- +8 reserved A100-equivalent GPUs (us-west primary).
- Throughput commitment: 450 req/min per pool; 99th pct token gen <=200ms.
- Bursting: automatic on-demand buffer up to 10% above reserved capacity, billed at on-demand rate ($/GPU-hour).
- Guardrails: if on-demand usage exceeds 30 consecutive minutes OR aggregate on-demand spend > $X/day, traffic will be routed to a read-only degraded pool and operations will trigger mitigations; SLA credit ladder applies if we miss latency SLO.
- Includes a 1-page runbook (attached) and a 2-hour playbook for critical incident response.

Option B — Economical baseline + soft-fallback:
- +4 reserved GPUs; higher on-demand headroom at standard on-demand pricing.
- System applies progressive request-prioritization; non-critical background jobs are deprioritized during peaks.
- No guaranteed 99th pct SLO; credits not applicable.

We can also commit to a signed addendum that defines the precise metering unit (GPU-second window, sample rate) so your finance team can forecast.

Attachments: [Attachment: SaaSify_Renewal_SOW_v3.pdf (PDF, 1.1MB)], [Attachment: SaaSify_Renewal_Redlines.docx (DOCX, 120KB)], [Attachment: SaaSify_Runbook_1p.pdf (PDF, 45KB)]

Next steps: pick Option A or B; legal will intake redlines. If Option A, we'll draft the SLA addendum and the credit ladder for signature. Can we lock this on Thurs 7/8?

Thanks,

Hannah —

Thanks for the clear options and the runbook. We reviewed with procurement and infra; we agree to move forward with Option A (firm-reserve + bounded failover) with one change request:

- Please include an explicit 10% burst allowance (as you proposed) but clarify that on-demand billing is per-minute metered in 60s windows and not per-request. We want a predictable billing unit.
- Add an explicit escalation action: after 30 consecutive minutes of on-demand usage, Redwood will notify SaaSify operations and begin a negotiated mitigation (either manual traffic shaping or crediting back a portion of on-demand spend if the issue is your side).
- Confirm that the 2-hour playbook includes a named on-call contact from Redwood and their escalation path.

Also procurement asked that we add a clause to the SOW about Marketplace credits (if applicable) and include a single signature block that allows SaaSify to approve via vendor portal.

If you can send the updated SOW and SLA addendum with the minute-metering language and named on-call, we can sign within 48 hours.

Appreciate the responsiveness — this should be straightforward.
